column1: # SC021 retirement / Stausland Johnsen split / SC040 move — formal interaction matrix.
# Produced by tools/cascade_interaction_harness.py (equivalence over the admitted
# proto input language, EnglishProtoInput .o. EARLIER .o. LATER vs the reverse),
# run inside the backend container against the post-repair germanic.txt.
# EARLIER = the rule that now executes first. See audits/sc021-adjudication.md §9a.
# Block 1: wiring of the new SC071/SC099/SC100 chain.
#   - SC071 (OELateOShortening, now *ō > *o) FEEDS both successors: noncommute.
#   - SC099 x SC100 commute: disjoint medial/final domains, no order claim needed.
#   - SC099 -> SC040 and SC100 -> SC040 are load-bearing: the computational image
#     of the 8th-c. (u/a split) vs 9th-c. (u > o lowering) stage contrast
#   - Fronting x SC071 now commutes: the old noncommute came solely from the
#     retired *ō > *a compression. SC071's late placement rests on Stausland
# Block 2: SC040 (OEMedUnstressedULowering) against every rule it jumped over in
# moving from before PWGmcFinalBareALoss to after the c.700 unstressed mergers.
# The five noncommuting pairs are exactly pairs where the jumped rule is a pre-OE
# or c.700 change and SC040 is 9th-c. — in each case the NEW order puts the
# historically earlier change first, i.e. the old position was formally
# load-bearing AND historically inverted (most sharply against OEIUmlaut and the
# syncopes). The 382-row corpus is output-identical under the move (fingerprints
# unchanged), so none of these five was distinguishing on current data.
